## The Boys' Dormitory corridor and Yuji's room

2 rows, each painted twice: the upstairs corridor of the boys' dormitory, with its seven doors, and Yuji's room off it. Nobody is in either picture.

Run this in the **local ComfyUI**. Press **Run** once.

Each row is one picture, painted twice: **version A** on top, **version B** under it. You choose between them afterwards.

The **Load Image** boxes on the left should already show their pictures. If one shows an error, click **choose file to upload** and pick the file with the same name from `JJK Game images/ui2/early`.

**Cost:** 4 pictures, about **$0.64** (Nano Banana Pro, about $0.16 a picture, charged to your Comfy account).

You don't need to save anything: the results go to ComfyUI's output folder and Claude picks them up from there.

If it stops with a rate-limit or "high demand" error, wait a minute and press **Run** again: a finished picture is reused, not paid for twice (as long as ComfyUI hasn't been restarted).

widgets_values: This is a background picture for a visual novel: a new picture of one room of a traditional Japanese mountain school, built of timber and white plaster. Picture 1 is the corridor of the other dormitory of this school, already painted: keep its camera, straight down the middle of the corridor, and keep the even spacing and the equal size of its six doors, three in each side wall, each facing the one opposite. The new picture is the corridor of a different house and differs as the words below say. Picture 2 is that house, cut from a picture already painted and seen from outside: two storeys of dark timber with a gallery along the upper floor. Picture 3 is a bedroom of the same house, already painted: the new corridor has the same pale plaster, dark timber posts, timber ceiling and polished timber floor. Do not copy the furniture of picture 3. THE PLACE: the upstairs corridor of the boys' dormitory, the house of dark timber of picture 2, seen straight down its middle from just inside its entrance. It is a straight, wide corridor, about three metres wide and twelve long, with walls of pale plaster between dark timber posts, a timber ceiling and a floor of polished timber boards. It has seven doors and no window. In the left wall are three doors and in the right wall three doors: six plain sliding doors of dark timber boards, all the same size, all shut, evenly spaced along the walls, each one facing the door opposite it, with the same width of plain plaster wall between each door and the next. In the middle of the far end wall is one more door of the same kind, shut. There is no window in either side wall and none in the end wall: the corridor is lit by a row of plain round lamps on the ceiling, which are on, and by daylight that comes in from behind me and lies along the floor. Against the left wall, near me and before the first door, stands a low open shoe rack with rows of shoes. On the far end wall, beside the door, hangs a notice board with small sheets of paper pinned to it and no writing that can be read. The corridor is empty and tidy, and its floor is clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture. The picture is seen from standing eye height, the horizon a little above the middle. Leave the right ninth of the picture and the top-left corner free of shelves and anything else one would walk to or use; the walls there are plain plaster and timber, fully painted. THE LOOK: a real place you could walk into, drawn as a clean modern anime background. Believable materials (wood grain, glass with soft reflections, stone, plaster, fabric), physically believable light with soft shadows and bounced light, real depth. Clean and well kept: walls are fresh and even, with no stains, cracks, peeling, damp patches or dirt, and there is no dust, litter or fallen leaves on the floor or the ground; everything that belongs to the place is still there. Crisp precise edges, clean clear colour, no film grain, no noise, no canvas texture, no visible brush strokes, no haze or glow washing out detail. Through every window a clear, in-focus view. No people, no animals, no text, no logos. Output a 16:9 picture.

Picture 1 is the dormitory garden, already painted: the same school. This room is upstairs in the house on the left of picture 1, and what is seen through its window is that garden from above. Picture 2 is that house, cut from picture 1 and seen from outside: dark timber, with a gallery and its rail along the upper floor. Picture 3 is another bedroom of the same house, already painted: the new room has the same pale plaster, dark timber posts, timber ceiling, polished timber floor and window frames. Do not copy the camera, the layout or the furniture of any of the three pictures: the new picture is taken indoors, in a different room. THE PLACE: a bedroom upstairs in the boys' dormitory, the house of dark timber of picture 2: a room given over to films. It is a tidy, cheerful room about five metres long and four wide. I stand inside at one end and look along the room. In the left wall, near me, is the door, a plain sliding door of dark timber boards, shut. Beyond the door, along the left wall, stands a low bed, neatly made, with a plain blanket and nothing lying on it. On the far wall hang film posters: bright pictures of cities, monsters and spaceships with no lettering on them. Under the posters, against the far wall and right of the middle, stands a shelf filled with rows of film cases, and beside it a small television on a low stand, switched off, with a round floor cushion on the floor in front of it. In the right wall, further along than the middle, is a wide window: through it I see the timber rail of the upstairs gallery just outside, the garden's pond below, and across the garden the white-plastered house with flower boxes under its windows. The stretch of the right wall nearest me is plain plaster. The floor is polished timber boards, clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture. The picture is seen from standing eye height, the horizon a little above the middle. Leave the right ninth of the picture and the top-left corner free of shelves and anything else one would walk to or use; the walls there are plain plaster and timber, fully painted.
